post.description: Simulates the deposit of an issued check. This API is always enabled, and is not affected by the operating hours of the sandbox Fed Check21 system.
Creates a sandbox card program for issuing simulation workflows.
Closes a sandbox card program for issuing simulation workflows.

Simulate a capture that converts an authorization hold into a settled transaction. The original transaction must have
started as an authorization and have an active hold.

Set `is_partial_capture` to `true` to keep the remaining hold active for future captures, as with split shipments; the
amount must not exceed the remaining authorized amount. Otherwise the capture is final and releases the remaining hold,
and the amount may exceed the authorized amount, as with tips or hotel incidentals.

Simulate an incremental authorization that adds to an existing authorization hold, such as a hotel stay extension.
Currency codes are preserved from the initial authorization.

The original transaction must have started as an authorization, not a full financial transaction, and must not have
captured funds. Column sends a real-time authorization decision request for the increment to your endpoint subscribed
to `decision.issuing.card_transaction`, and declines if none is configured.

Simulate a merchandise return against a settled card transaction. Each call creates a new refund transaction linked to
the purchase by `original_card_transaction_id`, and the total refunded must not exceed the settled amount.

Simulate an acquirer reversing the message that opened a card transaction, as with a voided sale or a
terminal that never got its authorization response. The transaction must have started as an authorization
or a full financial transaction.

Omit `cardholder_amount` to reverse in full: an authorization releases whatever hold the series still
carries, including incremental authorizations, and a full financial transaction reverses its settled
amount. Set `cardholder_amount` to release part of an authorization hold and leave the rest active, as
with a partially filled order; partial reversals don't apply to full financial transactions.

Reversals act on the outstanding authorization hold, so a transaction that has already been captured has
nothing left to reverse — refund it instead.

Simulate a card authorization for a sandbox card. The cardholder is always billed in `USD`; when `merchant_currency`
is not `USD`, provide `cardholder_fx_rate`.

When neither `realtime_decision` nor `network_standin` is set, Column sends a real-time authorization decision request
to your endpoint subscribed to `decision.issuing.card_transaction`, and declines if none is configured. Set
`realtime_decision` to supply the decision without calling your endpoint, or `network_standin` to simulate the card
network deciding on your behalf. To attach 3DS authentication details, pass an `authenticated` `three_ds_attempt_id`
for the same card.

To test PIN outcomes on a physical card, pass the PIN the cardholder enters in `cardholder_input.pin`. Column checks
it with its real PIN verification and lockout, so a wrong PIN declines with `pin_invalid`, a card with no PIN with
`pin_not_set`, and a card whose PIN is blocked after 3 wrong PINs with `pin_blocked`.

To test card-present and card-not-present decisioning, set `entry_mode` to `swipe`, `keyed` or `ecommerce`. By
default a physical card is swiped and a virtual card is used at an online checkout. Virtual cards only support
`ecommerce`, and a PIN can't be entered with `ecommerce`.

To test CVV2 outcomes, pass the CVV2 the cardholder enters in `cardholder_input.cvv2` with `entry_mode` `keyed` or
`ecommerce` (a virtual card's default). Column checks it with its real CVV2 verification, so a wrong CVV2 declines
with `invalid_cvv2`. When omitted, the card's real CVV2 is sent. A swiped card carries no CVV2.

To test expiration date outcomes, pass the date the cardholder presents in `cardholder_input.expiration_date`.
Column compares it with the card's expiration, so a date that doesn't match declines with `invalid_expiration`.
Without it, the simulated transaction carries no expiration date and Column skips the check.

To test address verification (AVS), pass the billing address the cardholder enters in
`cardholder_input.billing_address`. Column compares it with the cardholder entity's address and reports each
field as `verified` or `invalid` in the transaction's `cardholder_verification_details`. AVS doesn't decline
the authorization by itself.

Simulate a full financial transaction for a sandbox card. Full financial transactions capture funds immediately without
a prior authorization hold, as with transit taps, low-value purchases, and offline transactions. The cardholder is
always billed in `USD`; when `merchant_currency` is not `USD`, provide `cardholder_fx_rate`.

When `realtime_decision` is not set, Column sends a real-time authorization decision request to your endpoint
subscribed to `decision.issuing.card_transaction`, and declines if none is configured. Set `realtime_decision` to
supply the decision without calling your endpoint.

To test PIN outcomes on a PIN debit purchase with a physical card, pass the PIN the cardholder enters in
`cardholder_input.pin`. Column checks it with its real PIN verification and lockout, so a wrong PIN declines with
`pin_invalid`, a card with no PIN with `pin_not_set`, and a card whose PIN is blocked after 3 wrong PINs with
`pin_blocked`.

On a virtual card, `cardholder_input.cvv2` sets the CVV2 the cardholder enters, and a wrong CVV2 declines with
`invalid_cvv2`.

`cardholder_input.expiration_date` sets the expiration date the cardholder presents, and a date that doesn't match
the card's declines with `invalid_expiration`.

To test address verification (AVS), pass the billing address the cardholder enters in
`cardholder_input.billing_address`, as on an authorization. AVS doesn't decline the transaction by itself.

Simulate a 3DS authentication attempt for a sandbox card and return the resulting 3DS attempt.

Set `realtime_decision` to supply the authentication decision without calling your endpoint. When it is omitted, Column
sends a 3DS authentication decision request to your endpoint subscribed to `decision.issuing.card_authentication`; if
no endpoint is subscribed, the simulator creates an OTP challenge.

- `frictionless_approve` authenticates the attempt and fires `issuing.3ds.authentication_completed`.

ACHPositivePayRuleResponse.description: The ACH Positive Pay Rule object represents a whitelist rule for handling incoming debits. Incoming debits to a bank account with at least one positive pay rule will be automatically returned unless the incoming debit meets the conditions of a positive pay rule on the account. A positive pay rule is uniquely identified by the target bank account and the ACH Company ID present in an incoming debit.

ach_company_id.description: The ACH Company ID for the rule. This is a ten digit identifier.

ach_positive_pay_rule_id.description: The unique ID of the ACH positive pay rule

amount.description: the amount threshold in cents that will be used in rule evaluation. Must not be set if `amount_condition` is set to `ANY_AMOUNT`

amount_condition.description: This required field configures the rule to make a specific kind of amount comparison. equal: The incoming debit will only be permitted if the transfer amount equals the rule amount. `less_than_or_equal_to`: The incoming debit will only be permitted if the transfer amount is less than or equal to the rule amount. `any_amount`: The incoming debit will be permitted for any amount.

bank_account_id.description: ID of the bank account this rule applies to

description.description: Description of the rule. Maximum length: `255` characters.

ACHReturn.description: The ACH return object represents the current state of a single ACH return originated by or received by Column. The ACH return object will contain all relevant information about the specific return, which are described in the parameters below.

ach_transfer_id.description: The id of the ACH transfer that is being returned

created_at.description: The timestamp at which the return was created

details.description: Includes an object containing detailed information about the return

is_incoming.description: Indicates if the return was initiated by an RDFI ( `true` ) or by Column ( `false` ).

status.description: The current state of the ACH return. The possible states are `INITIATED`, `SENT`, `DISHONORED`, `CONTESTED`, `COMPLETED`, and `REJECTED`.

updated_at.description: The timestamp at which the return was updated (typically a status update)

addenda.description: Optional information provided about the ACH return

created_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH return is created

description.description: Description of the ACH return

status.description: Status of the ACH return

updated_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH return is updated

has_more.description: Whether additional returns exist beyond this page

ACHTransfer.description: The ACH transfer object represents the current state of a single ACH transfers originated by or received by Column. The ACH object will contain all relevant information about the specific transfer, which are described in the parameters below.

account_number_id.description: ID of the account number that is sending the transfer

ach_transfer_batch_id.description: ID of the ACH transfer batch this transfer belongs to.

acknowledged_at.description: The timestamp at which an acknowledgement is received for a `CCD` or `CTX` ACH transfer.

allow_overdraft.description: Allow the account to go negative for the transfer. The bank account needs to have `is_overdraftable` enabled with an overdraft reserve account linked to it.

amount.description: Amount (in cents) of the funds that will be transferred between originator and counterparty accounts. e.g. $1.75 would be represented by 175.

bank_account_id.description: ID of the bank account that is sending the transfer

cancelled_at.description: The timestamp at which the transfer is cancelled

company_discretionary_data.description: This optional field allows you to include codes (one or more), of significance only to you, to enable specialized handling of the transfer. There is no standardized interpretation for the value of the field. Maximum length: `20` characters. CIE: This field may contain the Biller's name. CTX: The Originator's bank account number may be placed in this field.

company_entry_description.description: You can use this optional field to provide the Receiver with a description of the purpose of the transfer. For example, "Gas bill", "Reg. Salary", "ins. prem.", "Soc. Sec.", "DTC", "Trade Pay", "PURCHASE", etc. Default value: `PAYMENT`. Maximum length: `10` characters.

company_id.description: Typically, a 10-digit unique identifier used for identifying entities, called originators, sending or collecting payments via ACH credit or ACH debit. For WEB entries it can be alphanumeric and less than 10 characters. If you would like to use a specific company ID when originating ACH transactions, please contact us.

company_name.description: The name of the originator company that initiated the ACH transfer

completed_at.description: The timestamp at which the 60 day return window has passed for this ACH transfer, and it is officially completed

counterparty_id.description: ID of the counterparty that will receive the transfer

created_at.description: The timestamp at which the transfer request is created

created_by.description: The identity (API key or dashboard user) that created the ACH transfer.

currency_code.description: The three-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217. e.g. `USD`.

description.description: Description of the transfer visible only in your platform. Maximum length: `255` characters.

effective_on.description: Datetime (00:00AM in Pacific Time zone) on which the transfer is effective. For incoming transfers, this is 00:00AM on the Settlement Date of the transfer in PT timezone.

entry_class_code.description: Standard Entry Class code of the transfer

entry_details.description: ACH entry details containing transaction code information

hold_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH transfer was placed on hold.

iat.description: This field provides additional IAT (International ACH Transfer) addenda information

id.description: The unique id for this object

idempotency_key.description: The idempotency key specified in the ACH transfer

initiated_at.description: The timestamp at which Column received your ACH request

intermediary_financial_institutions.description: Applies only to IAT transfers. This is a List of intermediary institutions involved in an IAT transfer.

is_incoming.description: Indicates whether the ACH transfer was incoming ( `true` ) or outgoing ( `false` ).

is_on_us.description: Indicates whether or not the ACH transfer is coming from a Column bank account. If `true` the request is processed immediately like a book transfer, and not sent to the Fed.

manual_review_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH transfer went into the manual review state

notification_of_changes.description: Details of Notifications of Change (NOCs), including corrected counterparty information and transaction codes. Available only with ach.`outgoing_transfer`.noc events.

nsf_deadline.description: For incoming ACH Debits and available only with ach.`incoming_transfer`.nsf events. This is the deadline by which the receiver account must be funded to complete the incoming debit. Column will file an NSF return for this ACH transfer if the account is not funded by the `nsf_deadline`.

odfi_routing_number.description: The externally facing routing number for the ODFI that initiated the ACH Transfer

payment_related_info.description: Provides additional information on the ACH transfer. Limited to 80 characters for most transfer types, but CTX transfers can include up to 799,920 characters (9,999 addenda records x 80 characters each). ENR and TRX transfers may also support extended lengths.

pre_review_at.description: The timestamp at which transfer approval became required for the ACH transfer.

receiver_id.description: This field contains the accounting reference number by which the Receiver is known to the Originator. It is included for further identification and for descriptive purposes. For example, it may be the number shown on an invoice, statement, billhead, notice, or other communication as the reference for the Receiver to update account receivable records.

receiver_name.description: The name of the receiver, usually the name on the bank account of the Receiver. Default value: beneficiary name of the counterparty. Maximum length: `22` characters.

return_contested_at.description: The timestamp at which the dishonored return for this transfer was contested by the RDFI

return_details.description: Details of the return processing history (e.g., initiated, dishonored, dishonor contested, manual review, etc.). Available only with ach.*.returned , ach.*.`return_dishonored` or ach.*.`return_contested` events.

return_dishonored_at.description: The timestamp at which the return for this transfer was dishonored by the ODFI

return_dishonored_funds_unlocked_at.description: The timestamp at which the dishonored return funds are unlocked

returned_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH transfer is returned by the RDFI

reversal_pair_transfer_id.description: If the transfer is the original transfer of an ACH Reversal, this field is the unique ID of the reversal transfer. If the transfer is the reversal transfer of an ACH Reversal, this field is the unique ID of the original transfer.

reviews.description: The transfer approval decisions recorded on the ACH transfer. Each entry is a dashboard user approving or rejecting the transfer while it was in `pre_review`. This list is only populated when transfer approvals are enabled for the platform, or for the API key that created the transfer; otherwise it is omitted from the response.

same_day.description: Specify if the transfer is a same-day ACH transfer. If it is set as `true`, it takes precedence over `effective_date` and overrides it.

settled_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH was settled

status.description: The current state of the ACH transfer. Possible values: `PRE_REVIEW`, `INITIATED`, `HOLD`, `PENDING_SUBMISSION`, `SUBMITTED`, `SETTLED`, `RETURNED`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELED`, `SCHEDULED`, `PENDING_RETURN`, `RETURN_DISHONORED`, `RETURN_DISHONORED_FUNDS_UNLOCKED`, `RETURN_CONTESTED`, `MANUAL_REVIEW`, and `MANUAL_REVIEW_APPROVED`.

submitted_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH transfer was submitted to the Fed

trace_number.description: The unique number assigned to every ACH entry by an ODFI which identifies that entry within a specific ACH file

transaction_type_code.description: This is a required code on IAT transfers used to identify reason for payment. Possible values: `ANN`, `BUS`, `DEP`, `LOA`, `MIS`, `MOR`, `PEN`, `REM`, `RLS`, `SAL`, `TAX`.

type.description: ACH transfer type: `CREDIT` or `DEBIT`. [Learn more]({{ach}}).

ultimate_beneficiary_counterparty_id.description: ID of the ultimate beneficiary counterparty that will receive the transfer. This is only required on outgoing IAT debits.

ultimate_originator_counterparty_id.description: ID of the ultimate originating counterparty that sent the transfer. This is only required on outgoing IAT credits.

updated_at.description: The timestamp at which the ACH transfer was last updated

has_more.description: Whether there are more results available after this set.

available_amount.description: The amount available for immediate use, in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for `USD`).

holding_amount.description: The amount on hold and not available for use, in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for `USD`).

locked_amount.description: The amount locked due to overdraft coverage, in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for `USD`).

pending_amount.description: The amount of pending transactions that have not yet settled, in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for `USD`).

AccountNumber.description: An account number that routes incoming payments to a bank account.

bank_account_id.description: The bank account this account number is associated with

check_issuing_manual_settlement_required.description: Whether manual settlement is required for check issuing

check_issuing_positive_pay_required.description: Whether check issuing positive pay is required

check_issuing_prefund_required.description: Whether prefund is required for check issuing. `null` inherits the platform default.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the account number was created

description.description: A description for this account number

id.description: Unique identifier for the account number

ActivityLineItemResponse.description: A single line of activity on a bank account, as it would appear on a bank statement. Amounts are in the smallest unit of the bank account's currency, which the list response returns as `currency_code`; line items do not carry a currency of their own. Transfers in a batch that is rolled up on statements, such as a check deposit batch, appear as one line item per batch per day (UTC) instead of one per transfer, with credits and debits as separate line items.

activity_line_item_id.description: The ID of the activity line item, prefixed with `lent_`. Use it as the `starting_after` or `ending_before` cursor to paginate.

amount.description: The signed amount of the activity in the smallest unit of the bank account's currency (e.g., cents for `USD`). Credits are positive and debits are negative. For a rolled-up batch, the sum of the batch's transfers that posted that day.

bank_account_id.description: The ID of the bank account the activity belongs to.

description.description: A human-readable description of the activity. For a rolled-up batch that settled across more than one day, it ends with `(partial batch, part settled on M/D/YY)`.

running_balance.description: The bank account's balance immediately after the activity posted, in the smallest unit of the bank account's currency (e.g., cents for `USD`).

settlement_date.description: The time the activity posted to the bank account. For a rolled-up batch, the time the last of the batch's transfers that day posted.

transaction_id.description: The ID of the transfer that produced the activity. For a rolled-up batch, the ID of the transfer batch (`tbat_…`).

type.description: The kind of activity, as shown on bank statements. `ACH Batch`, `Check Deposit Batch`, and `Check Issuance Batch` are rolled-up batches.

entity_id.description: The entity ID to add as owner

document_id.description: The ID of a document uploaded via `POST /issuing/card-disputes/documents`. Documents uploaded via `POST /documents` are rejected.

narrative.example: The cardholder did not authorize this transaction and still has the card.

reason_details.description: Normalized reason-specific details for the dispute.

reason_for_partial_dispute.description: Reason the cardholder is disputing less than the full transaction amount. Required at submission when the dispute amount is less than the transaction amount, except for `incorrect_amount` disputes, which are partial by nature: for those the value is stored but never required or sent to the network.

branch_country_code.description: The two-character country code of the foreign correspondent bank

identification_number.description: The identification number of the foreign correspondent bank

identification_number_qualifier.description: The numbering scheme used in the identification number. Possible values are `01` (National Clearing System Number), `02` (BIC Code), or `03` (IBAN).

name.description: The name of the foreign correspondent bank

intermediary_bank.description: The amended BIC of the intermediary bank.

message_to_beneficiary_bank.description: The amended free-form message to the beneficiary bank.

purpose_codes.description: The amended list of purpose codes for the transfer.

remittance_beneficiary_reference.description: The amended remittance reference identifying the beneficiary's invoice or payment.

amended_fields.description: The fields that were actually amended with their new values.

request_summary.description: A summary of the amendment request.

requested_at.description: The timestamp when the amendment was requested.

requested_fields.description: List of field names that were requested to be amended.

sent_at.description: The timestamp when the amendment was sent.

amount.description: Amount of locked collateral to apply to loan principal, in cents.

ownership_percentage.description: The percentage of ownership the person holds in the business (0-100).

overdraft_amount.description: The amount that has been locked or released in the reserve account.

transfer_id.description: ID of transfer that triggered this alert.

available_balance_credit.description: Total credit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `available_balance`. Zero or positive.

available_balance_debit.description: Total debit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `available_balance`. Zero or negative.

holding_balance_close.description: Close `holding_balance` in the currency's smallest unit at the end of `effective_on` in `time_zone`.

holding_balance_credit.description: Total credit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `holding_balance`. Zero or positive.

holding_balance_debit.description: Total debit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `holding_balance`. Zero or negative.

locked_balance_close.description: Close `locked_balance` in the currency's smallest unit at the end of `effective_on` in `time_zone`.

locked_balance_debit.description: Total debit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `locked_balance`. Zero or negative.

pending_balance_debit.description: Total debit amount in the currency's smallest unit applied to `pending_balance`. Zero or negative.

transaction_count.description: Total number of transactions on the day of `effective_on`.

BankAccountWithDetails.description: A bank account is the object in the Column data model that has the ability to hold, send, and receive funds. Bank accounts are children of entities. An entity can have multiple bank accounts. Bank accounts can have one or multiple account numbers. Read about bank accounts in our data model section for more information.

balances.description: Lists all possible balance amounts for an account represented in the smallest unit of the currency.

bic.description: The SWIFT BIC code for this bank account for international wire payments.

created_at.description: The timestamp at which the bank account was created.

currency_code.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the account and its balances.

default_account_number.description: The externally facing default account number tied to this bank account.

default_account_number_id.description: The default account number ID tied to this account.

description.description: A name for the bank account (minimum: 3 characters)

display_name.description: The display name for the bank account. Display name is an account nickname used on Column's Dashboard.

fdic_insurance.description: The type of FDIC insurance offered on this account. The default value is `standard`.

id.description: Unique ID for this account.

interest_config_id.description: The ID of interest config for this account. If it is not set, the default interest config of your platform will be used for this account. Please contact our support team for more details.

is_interest_bearing.description: Whether your platform needs to accrue and pay interest to this account. Please contact our support team for more details.

is_overdraftable.description: Whether the account can be overdrafted, must include an `overdraft_reserve_account_id`

overdraft_reserve_account_id.description: The overdraft reserve account that this account is linked to. If `is_overdraftable`: `true` then this field is required.

owners.description: List of `entity_id`'s which are tied to this bank account

routing_number.description: The 9-digit ABA routing number for this bank account.

status.description: The current status of the bank account. Can be `open`, `closed`, or `frozen`.

type.description: Bank Account type. Can be `CHECKING`, `OVERDRAFT_RESERVE`, `PROGRAM_RESERVE`, or `NETWORK_SETTLEMENT_ACCOUNT`.

BookTransfer.description: The book transfer object is the current state of a single book transfer initiated in Column. A book transfer is the movement of funds between two bank accounts under your platform, and once initiated, happen instantaneously 24/7.

allow_overdraft.description: Allows the account to go negative for an outgoing transfer. The bank account needs to have `is_overdraftable` enabled with an overdraft reserve account linked to it

amount.description: Amount (in cents) of the funds that will be transferred between sender and receiver accounts. e.g. $1.75 would be represented by 175.

created_at.description: The timestamp at which the transfer request is created

currency_code.description: The three-letter currency code defined in ISO 4217. e.g. `USD`

description.description: A description of the transfer visible in account statements

id.description: The unique ID of the object

idempotency_key.description: The idempotency key specified in the book transfer

receiver_account_number_id.description: ID of the account number that will receive the transfer

receiver_bank_account_id.description: ID of the bank account that will receive the transfer

sender_account_number_id.description: ID of the account number that is sending the transfer

sender_bank_account_id.description: ID of the bank account that is sending the transfer

status.description: The current status of the book transfer. Possible values: `REJECTED`, `COMPLETED`, `HOLD`, and `CANCELED`.

updated_at.description: The timestamp at which the book transfer was updated (typically a status update)

has_more.description: Whether more book transfers are available

authorization_method.description: The method used to authorize the book transfer.

merchant_category_code.description: The merchant category code (MCC) associated with this transfer.

merchant_name.description: The merchant name associated with this transfer.

sender_name.description: Name of the sender initiating the transfer.

statement_description.description: Description that will appear on the account statement.

website.description: Website associated with the transfer originator.

account_usage.description: Indicates possible uses of the accounts an entity may use at Column. Only required for a root entity.

address.description: The physical address where the business operates. Addresses need to adhere to character validation, as addresses are used across multiple payment rails. Characters are validated according to the Fedwire character validation.

countries_of_operation.description: Countries in which the business currently operates or expects to operate. Only ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 Country Codes (e.g., `US`, `FR`, `UK`, `DE`, ... ) are allowed. Only required for a root entity.

country_of_incorporation.description: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code of the country in which the business is incorporated.

dba_name.description: "Doing business as" name for the business entity, when different from the legal business name.

description.description: Description of the business entity. Only required for a root entity.

ein.description: Employer Identification Number (Tax ID). This may be SSN for a sole proprietorship.

ein_pending.description: Indicates whether the business has applied for an EIN but has not yet received it.

end_customer_type.description: Type of end customer the business serves. Accepts a free-form string.

expected_payment_rails.description: Expected transaction types for the account. Comma-separated list of payment rails; each value must be one of: `ach`, `wire`, `swift`, `check`, `rtp`, `card_spend`.

expected_use_of_funds.description: Expected use of funds for the business entity. Accepts a free-form string.

has_virtual_address.description: Indicates whether the business operates from a virtual address.

industry.description: Industry in which the business entity operates.

is_high_risk.description: Indicates whether the entity has been identified as high risk based on compliance screening

legal_type.description: Type of business. Permitted values are `limited-partnership`, `trust`, `sole-proprietorship`, `corporation`, `llc`, `general-partnership`, `professional-association`, `government`, `non-profit`, `other`, `pic-piv`, `spv`, `irrevocable_trust`, `revocable_trust`.

makes_international_payments.description: Indicates whether the business expects to make international payments.

payment_volumes.description: Expected payment volumes. Only required for a root entity.

registration_id.description: Registration ID. EIN or Registration ID is required.

source_of_funds.description: Source of funds for the business entity.

state_of_incorporation.description: State in which the business is incorporated. Only postal abbreviations (e.g. `AL`, `CA`, `DE`, ...) are allowed. Only required for a root entity.

website.description: Website of the business. Optional, but highly encouraged as it will increase likelihood of an automated verification.

year_of_incorporation.description: Year in which the business entity was incorporated. Only required for a root entity.

cancellation_reason.description: The reason for canceling the transfer. Possible values: `incorrect_amount`, `incorrect_currency`, `requested_by_originator`, `duplicate`, `fraud`, `tech_failure`, `payment_not_justified`.

Card.description: The card object represents a payment card attached to a card account.

authorized_user_entity_id.description: The ID of the person entity authorized to use this card

bin.description: The 6 or 8-digit BIN (Bank Identification Number) for the card

card_account_id.description: The ID of the card account

card_authorization_policy_id.description: The ID of the card authorization policy

card_program_id.description: The ID of the card program

card_template_id.description: The ID of the card template the physical card was created with: the `card_template_id` from the create request, or the card program's default card template when none was given. Renewed and replaced cards keep the original card's template. This field is `null` for virtual cards.

created_at.description: The creation date of the card

deactivated_at.description: The timestamp when the card was deactivated

deactivation_reason.description: The reason this card was deactivated. Null until deactivation. When a card is replaced, this reason is recorded on the original card, not the new replacement card. Historical cards may return an inferred reason; generic legacy deactivations are reported as `voluntary`.

description.description: A description for this card. Empty when unset. Renewed and replaced cards keep the original card's description.

expiration_month.description: The expiration month of the card (1-12)

expiration_year.description: The expiration year of the card (4-digit year, e.g. 2025)

first_activated_at.description: The timestamp when the card was first activated

id.description: The ID of the card

last_active_at.description: Timestamp when the card was last set to active status

last_four_digits.description: The last four digits of the card PAN

last_inactive_at.description: Timestamp when the card was last set to deactivated status

last_paused_at.description: Timestamp when the card was last set to paused status

manufacturing_details.description: Manufacturing and shipping details for physical cards. This field is `null` for virtual cards

original_card_id.description: The ID of the card that this card replaced. Populated on the replacement card

pin_status.description: The state of the card's PIN. `set`: the card has a PIN. A debit card created with an `encrypted_pin` or `generate_pin`, or renewed from a card that had a PIN, has one, and setting a PIN later also moves it to `set`. `unset`: the card has no PIN, and transactions that require a PIN decline with `pin_not_set`. Always `unset` for non-debit cards. `blocked`: the card has a PIN, but it is locked after too many wrong attempts. A PIN carried over on renewal or replacement starts unblocked, even if the original card's PIN was blocked.

platform_id.description: The ID of the platform that owns this card

replacement_card_id.description: The ID of the card that replaced this one. Populated on the original card after replacement

sequence_number.description: The sequence number of the card. Starts at 1 for new cards and increments when a card is renewed (same PAN, new expiration). Resets to 1 when a card is replaced (new PAN)

status.description: The current status of the card. Possible values: `active`, `paused`, `deactivated`

type.description: The form factor of the card. Possible values: `virtual`, `physical`.

CardAccount.description: The card account object represents a card account in your platform.

bank_account_id.description:
The ID of the associated bank account, if any. For a `cardholder_secured` account,
this is the secured loan's collateral bank account and is set automatically at creation.

card_program_id.description: The ID of the card program

closed_at.description: The closed date of the card account

last_opened_at.description: The last opened date of the card account

last_suspended_at.description: The last suspended date of the card account

loan_id.description: The ID of the associated loan (if any)

status.description: The status of the card account

channel.description: The transaction channel supplied by the 3DS network

merchant_challenge_indicator.description: The raw EMV 3DS merchant challenge indicator

network_risk_score.description: The network-provided risk score for this authentication, forwarded unmodified: a one- or two-digit numeric string from 0 to 99.

decision.description: The authentication decision. Possible values: frictionless_approve, challenge, decline_authentication

decline_reason.description: The optional decline reason. When omitted for a declined authentication, Column defaults to suspected_fraud

CardAuthenticationDecisionThreeDSAttempt.description: A 3D Secure authentication attempt included in an authentication decision request

acs_transaction_id.description: The Access Control Server (ACS) transaction identifier

amount.description: The transaction amount in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for `USD`)

attempt_count.description: The number of authentication attempts made

attempt_status.description: The current status of the 3DS authentication attempt

card_account_id.description: The card account associated with this 3DS attempt

card_id.description: The card associated with this 3DS attempt

challenged_at.description: Timestamp when the challenge was presented to the cardholder

challenges_presented.description: List of challenge types that were presented to the cardholder

chosen_challenge.description: The challenge type selected by the cardholder

currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction

merchant_country_code.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the merchant

outcome_reason.description: The reason for the authentication outcome

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the 3DS attempt was last updated

checking.description: Balances of the bank account linked to the card account.

collateral.description: Balances of the loan's collateral bank account. Included for secured credit accounts.

credit.description: The underlying loan's balances, before collateral restrictions or other card spend adjustments.

CardAuthorizationDecisionBankAccountBala.description: Raw bank account balances in the smallest unit of currency_code.

currency_code.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the bank account and its balances.

holding_amount.description: The bank account's balance held for pending transactions.

CardAuthorizationDecisionCreditBalances.description: Raw loan balances in the smallest unit of currency_code.

currency_code.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code of the loan and its balances.

max_principal_balance.description: The configured credit limit of the card account's underlying loan.

principal_holding.description: The loan's principal held for pending transactions.

available_balance.description: The card account's available balance when Column requests the realtime authorization decision. When Column limits the proposed event to available funds, this is the maximum amount the platform may partially approve

balances.description: Raw balances of the accounts backing the card. Only applicable account groups are included, when Column has loaded a balance snapshot. Amounts are in the smallest unit of each group's currency.

card.description: The card used for the transaction, as it is when Column requests the decision. This is the same object returned by the card endpoints, so it includes the card's status and pin_status

card_transaction.description: The card transaction being authorized. For new transactions, this will be a new transaction object. For incremental authorizations or reauthorizations, this will contain the existing card transaction

proposed_event.description: The proposed card transaction event that Column is requesting a decision on. This event will be appended to the card transaction if approved

decision.description: The authorization decision. Possible values: approve, partially_approve, decline

decline_reason.description: Optional reason for the decline. Providing a decline reason helps merchants understand why the transaction was declined and can reduce network fees. If not specified, Column will return a generic do not honor response code. Possible values: insufficient_funds, suspected_fraud, stop_payment, require_3ds

funding_account_id.description: The ID of a bank account on your platform to just-in-time fund the authorization from. Only applicable when decision is approve or partially_approve on an initial purchase authorization on a debit card program with jit_funding_enabled. If the card account's available balance does not cover the approved amount, Column moves the shortfall, plus any amount the card account is overdrawn, from this account into the card account's bank account before approving; the funding is recorded in the card transaction's funding_details and returned to this account, up to the amount the authorization releases, if the authorization is reversed, expires, or clears for less. If this account cannot cover the shortfall, the authorization is declined

partially_approve_amount.description: The amount to partially approve in the smallest unit of the currency (e.g., cents for USD). Only applicable when decision is partially_approve. The request must support partial approvals (check can_support_partial_approvals in the point of sale details). If partial approval is not supported, the transaction will be declined. Incremental authorizations and reauthorizations do not support partial approval

CardAuthorizationPolicy.description: The config object contains the rules and limits that define what transactions are allowed or blocked.

allowed_merchant_category_codes.description: List of allowed merchant category codes (MCCs). If specified, only transactions with these MCCs will be allowed

allowed_merchant_country_codes.description: List of allowed merchant country codes. If specified, only transactions from these countries will be allowed

allowed_merchant_currency_codes.description: List of allowed merchant currency codes. If specified, only transactions in these currencies will be allowed

allowed_merchant_ids.description: List of allowed merchant identifiers. If specified, only transactions from these specific merchants will be allowed. Each identifier must be ASCII and at most 15 characters

blocked_merchant_category_codes.description: List of blocked merchant category codes (MCCs). Transactions with these MCCs will be declined

blocked_merchant_country_codes.description: List of blocked merchant country codes. Transactions from these countries will be declined

blocked_merchant_currency_codes.description: List of blocked merchant currency codes. Transactions in these currencies will be declined

blocked_merchant_ids.description: List of blocked merchant identifiers. Transactions from these specific merchants will be declined. Each identifier must be ASCII and at most 15 characters

card_spend_policies.description: List of spend policies that define volume and frequency limits

CardAuthorizationPolicyEvaluationDetail.description: The evaluation result of a single authorization policy

card_authorization_policy_id.description: The ID of the card authorization policy

card_authorization_policy_version_id.description: The ID of the card authorization policy version

decision.description: The policy evaluation decision. Possible values: `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`

decision_reason.description: The reason the policy failed. Only set when decision is failed

owner.description: The owner of the policy. Possible values: `column`, `platform_owner`

scope.description: The scope of the policy. Possible values: `card_program`, `card_account`, `card`

CardAuthorizationPolicyVersion.description: The card authorization policy version object represents a specific version of an authorization policy that controls which card transactions are allowed or blocked.

card_authorization_policy_id.description: The ID of the parent card authorization policy

config.description: Policy configuration containing rules and limits

created_at.description: Creation timestamp

effective_on.description: When this policy version becomes effective

id.description: The ID of the card authorization policy version

scope.description: The scope of this authorization policy (program, account, or card).

bin_lower_bound_inclusive.description: The lower bound of the BIN range (inclusive)

bin_upper_bound_inclusive.description: The upper bound of the BIN range (inclusive)

id.description: The ID of the BIN range

is_active.description: Whether this BIN range is active

scheme.description: The card scheme for this BIN range

allowed_close_resolutions.description: Close resolutions Column will currently accept via POST /close, given the dispute's stage, workflow, and network state. Empty when no new close is possible.

allowed_response_actions.description: Response actions Column will currently accept via POST /respond, given the dispute's stage, workflow, and network state. Empty when no response is possible.

amount.description: The dispute amount in smallest currency unit

card_account_id.description: The ID of the card account

card_program_id.description: The ID of the card program

card_transaction_id.description: The ID of the card transaction

compelling_evidence_certification_requir.description: Whether POST /respond currently requires `compelling_evidence_reviewed_with_cardholder` and `cardholder_name_and_address_mismatch`. True while you can decline or partially accept a fraud pre-arbitration in which the acquirer presented compelling evidence.

created_at.description: When the dispute was created

id.description: The ID of the card dispute

last_network_sync_at.description: When Column last synchronized the dispute's state from the network. This reflects Column's own sync job, not a live network read; refreshing the page does not force a new synchronization.

next_actions.description: Customer-visible next actions for the dispute.

provisional_credit.description: Whether a provisional credit has been issued for this dispute. Removing the credit while the dispute is a draft clears the flag. Otherwise it records credit issuance history: a reversal after the dispute is closed does not clear the flag, so outside of drafts it is not an indicator of a current outstanding credit balance.

reason_details.description: Normalized reason-specific details for the dispute.

reason_for_partial_dispute.description: Explanation of why the cardholder is disputing less than the full transaction amount, stored when the claim is partial. Not used for `incorrect_amount` disputes.

requested_resolution.description: Close resolution queued for a submitted dispute awaiting network recall, distinguishing saved close intent from a request the server never received.

resolution_reason.description: The resolution reason for the dispute

respond_by.description: The date by which the next network action is due.

stage.description: The current stage of the dispute

status.description: The public status of the dispute.

submission_error.description: The most recent network submission error. Populated only when submission_status is failed; never set for requires_action, which is a normal state in which the network is awaiting the platform's response.

submitted_at.description: When the dispute was submitted to the network. Null while the dispute has never been sent, including drafts and queued submissions.

updated_at.description: When the dispute was last updated

workflow.description: The Visa dispute workflow the dispute follows. Collaboration disputes negotiate through chargeback, representment, and pre-arbitration; allocation disputes cover fraud-related claims the acquirer responds to directly.

CardDisputeAccountStatus.description: The account condition that should have caused the authorization to be declined.

attempted_return_date.description: When did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.

canceled_before_shipping.description: Did the cardholder cancel before the merchandise shipped? Required when the cardholder canceled merchandise that was received.

cancellation_date.description: When did the cardholder cancel? Required when the cardholder canceled `timeshare` or `other` services, canceled merchandise that was not received, or canceled merchandise before it shipped, and for `properly_canceled` and `attempted_cancellation_within_24_hours` guaranteed reservations.

cancellation_method.description: How and why did the cardholder cancel? Required when the cardholder canceled `timeshare` or `other` services, canceled merchandise that was not received, or canceled merchandise before it shipped.
cancellation_method.example: The cardholder canceled by email to the merchant's support address.

cancellation_policy_provided.description: Was a cancellation policy provided? Required for merchandise that was not received or was canceled before it shipped, for `guaranteed_reservation` services, and for `timeshare` services canceled more than 14 days after `timeshare_date`.

cardholder_attempted_resolution.description: Did the cardholder attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant? Required.

cardholder_attempted_return.description: Did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when the merchandise was not returned.

cardholder_canceled.description: Did the cardholder cancel? Required for merchandise that was not received and for `timeshare` and `other` services, optional for merchandise that was received, and not used for `guaranteed_reservation` services. Must be true for `other` services.

cardholder_received_merchandise.description: Did the cardholder receive the merchandise? Required for merchandise.

cardholder_returned_merchandise.description: Did the cardholder return the merchandise? Required when `cardholder_received_merchandise` is true.

guaranteed_reservation_certification.description: What does the cardholder certify about the guaranteed reservation? Required for `guaranteed_reservation` services.

merchandise_disposition.description: What is the current disposition of the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.
merchandise_disposition.example: The cardholder still has the merchandise and can return it on request.

merchandise_or_services.description: Was the canceled purchase merchandise or services? Required.

merchant_accepted_cancellation.description: Did the merchant accept the cancellation? Required when the cardholder canceled `timeshare` or `other` services, or canceled merchandise before it shipped, no more than 15 days before submission.

merchant_received_return_date.description: When did the merchant receive the returned merchandise? Required when the merchandise was returned.

merchant_return_refusal_reason.description: Why did the merchant not provide or accept a merchandise return? Required when a return was attempted. Must be `refused_return_authorization`, `refused_accept_returned_merchandise` or `advised_not_to_return`.

order_details.description: What did the cardholder purchase? Required for merchandise and for `other` services.
order_details.example: A pair of running shoes ordered from the merchant's website.

received_or_expected_date.description: When did the cardholder receive the merchandise, or when did they expect to receive it? Required for merchandise.

resolution_prohibited_by_local_law.description: Is an attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant prohibited by local law or regulations? Required when `cardholder_attempted_resolution` is false. Must be true: Visa does not accept a dispute where the cardholder neither attempted resolution nor was prohibited from doing so.

return_attempt_details.description: How did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.
return_attempt_details.example: The cardholder requested a return label, but the merchant did not respond.

return_method.description: How was the merchandise returned? Required when the merchandise was returned.

return_method_details.description: How was the merchandise returned, when `return_method` is `other`? Required in that case.
return_method_details.example: The cardholder dropped the merchandise off at the merchant's retail store.

return_tracking_number.description: What is the shipment's tracking number? Optional. Sent to the network only when `return_method` is `fedex`, `dhl`, `ups`, `postal_service` or `other`.

returned_date.description: When did the cardholder return the merchandise? Required when the merchandise was returned.

service_date.description: When was the service provided, or when was it expected to be? Required for `guaranteed_reservation` and `other` services.

service_type.description: What type of service was canceled? Required for services.

timeshare_date.description: What is the date of the timeshare, or the date the contract or related documents were received? Required for `timeshare` services.

account_closure_date.description: The date the issuer informed the merchant that the account was closed. Provide either this or `cancellation_date`, not both. When provided, `cancellation_method`, `merchant_contact_methods` and the merchant contact details are not required.

cancellation_date.description: The date the cardholder canceled the recurring agreement with the merchant. Required unless `account_closure_date` is provided; the two cannot be combined.

cancellation_method.description: How the cardholder canceled the recurring agreement with the merchant. Required when `cancellation_date` is provided.
cancellation_method.example: The cardholder canceled by email to the merchant's support address.

merchant_contact_application_name.description: The name of the app or website through which the cardholder reached the merchant. Required when `merchant_contact_methods` includes `webform`.

merchant_contact_email_address.description: The email address the cardholder used to reach the merchant. Required when `merchant_contact_methods` includes `email`.

merchant_contact_methods.description: The channels the cardholder used to contact the merchant when canceling. At least one is required when `cancellation_date` is provided: Visa rejects a canceled-recurring-transaction dispute that asserts the cardholder contacted the merchant without naming a channel.

merchant_contact_phone_number.description: The phone number the cardholder used to reach the merchant. Required when `merchant_contact_methods` includes `call_center` or `sms`.

merchant_contact_physical_address.description: The address at which the cardholder reached the merchant. Required when `merchant_contact_methods` includes `mail` or `in_person`.

CardDisputeCloseResolution.description: How a dispute is resolved when the platform closes it in the cardholder's favor or the cardholder withdraws the claim.

CardDisputeCounterfeitMerchandiseReasonD.description: Details for a counterfeit-merchandise dispute. An uploaded document is required before submission.

counterfeit_details.description: How the cardholder determined the merchandise was counterfeit. Required.
counterfeit_details.example: The brand's authentication service confirmed the item is not genuine.

counterfeit_discovered_date.description: The date the cardholder discovered the merchandise was counterfeit. Required.

merchandise_disposition.description: Current disposition of the counterfeit merchandise. Required.
merchandise_disposition.example: The cardholder still has the merchandise and can return it on request.

order_details.example: A pair of running shoes ordered from the merchant's website.

CardDisputeCreditNotProcessedReasonDetai.description: Details for a credit-not-processed dispute. An uploaded document (the credit voucher, transaction receipt or refund acknowledgement) is required before submission.

canceled_or_returned_date.description: The date the cardholder canceled the service or returned the merchandise. Required when `credit_voucher_dated` is `false`.

credit_voucher_date.description: The date the merchant issued the credit voucher or transaction receipt that was never processed. Required unless `credit_voucher_dated` is `false`, in which case it is ignored.

credit_voucher_dated.description: Is the credit voucher, transaction receipt or refund acknowledgement dated? Defaults to `true` when omitted.

late_credit_explanation.description: Why was the credit issued late, and what are the details of the ongoing negotiations between the cardholder and the merchant? Required when `credit_voucher_date` (or `canceled_or_returned_date` for an undated voucher) is more than 113 days after the transaction was processed. CardDisputeCurrencyError.description: What was wrong with the transaction currency: processed in a different currency than agreed, or converted with dynamic currency conversion the cardholder did not agree to.

attempted_return_date.description: When did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.

cardholder_attempted_resolution.description: Did the cardholder attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant? Required.

cardholder_attempted_return.description: Did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when the merchandise was not returned.

cardholder_first_notified_issuer_date.description: When did the cardholder first notify the issuer of the dispute? Required when `previous_negotiation_evidence` is true.

cardholder_returned_merchandise.description: Did the cardholder return the merchandise? Required.

merchandise_disposition.description: What is the current disposition of the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.
merchandise_disposition.example: The cardholder still has the merchandise and can return it on request.

merchant_received_return_date.description: When did the merchant receive the returned merchandise? Required when the merchandise was returned.

merchant_return_refusal_reason.description: Why did the merchant not provide or accept a merchandise return? Required when a return was attempted.

negotiation_details.description: What were the previous ongoing negotiations between the cardholder and the merchant? Required when `previous_negotiation_evidence` is true.
negotiation_details.example: The cardholder emailed the merchant twice asking for a refund and received no response.

negotiation_start_date.description: When did the negotiations begin? Required when `previous_negotiation_evidence` is true.

order_details.description: What did the cardholder order, and how was it damaged or defective? Required.
order_details.example: A pair of running shoes ordered from the merchant's website.

previous_negotiation_evidence.description: Is there evidence of previous ongoing negotiations between the cardholder and the merchant? Required when both `received_date` and the transaction's processing date are more than 113 days before submission.

received_date.description: When did the cardholder receive the merchandise? Required.

resolution_prohibited_by_local_law.description: Is an attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant prohibited by local law or regulations? return_attempt_details.description: How did the cardholder attempt to return the merchandise? Required when a return was attempted.
return_attempt_details.example: The cardholder requested a return label, but the merchant did not respond.

return_method.description: How was the merchandise returned? Required when the merchandise was returned.

return_method_details.description: How was the merchandise returned, when `return_method` is `other`? Required in that case.
return_method_details.example: The cardholder dropped the merchandise off at the merchant's retail store.

return_tracking_number.description: What is the shipment's tracking number? Optional. Sent to the network only when `return_method` is `fedex`, `dhl`, `ups` or `postal_service`.

returned_date.description: When did the cardholder return the merchandise? Required when the merchandise was returned.

document_id.description: The ID of a document uploaded via `POST /issuing/card-disputes/documents`. Documents uploaded via `POST /documents` are rejected.

CardDisputeDuplicateProcessingReasonDeta.description: Details for a duplicate-processing dispute. `cash_receipt`, `cancelled_check`, `other_card_statement` and `other` proofs, and a `third_party_voucher` with `merchant_passed_on_funds_evidence`, require an uploaded document before submission.

merchant_passed_on_funds_evidence.description: Does the issuer have evidence that the first merchant passed on the funds to the second merchant? Required when `other_payment_proof` is `third_party_voucher`. Visa blocks the dispute unless it does, so `false` is rejected.

other_acquirer_reference_number.description: What is the other transaction's acquirer reference number? Required when `other_payment_proof` is `acquirer_reference_number`. 23 or 24 digits.

other_card_transaction_id.description: Which card transaction is the other charge? Required when `other_transaction_on_same_card` or `other_transaction_on_different_card` is true. It must belong to this platform, be on the same card number as the disputed transaction when `other_transaction_on_same_card` is true and on a different card number otherwise, and carry a Visa transaction identifier.

other_network_transaction_id.description: What is the other transaction's Visa transaction identifier? Required when `other_payment_proof` is `network_transaction_id`. 15 digits, or 17 with a multiple clearing sequence number.

other_payment_proof.description: What proof of the payment by other means is available? Required when `other_transaction_paid_by_other_means` is true.

other_transaction_on_different_card.description: Is the other transaction for the same merchant and on a different Visa card of the same cardholder? Required when `other_transaction_on_same_card` is false.

other_transaction_on_same_card.description: Are both transactions for the same merchant and on the same card? Required. A renewed or damaged-card replacement that keeps the card number is the same card.

other_transaction_paid_by_other_means.description: Was the other transaction paid by other means? Required when the other transaction is on neither card. Visa blocks the dispute unless it was, so `false` is rejected.

amount.description: The dispute amount in smallest currency unit.

card_transaction_id.description: The ID of the card transaction to dispute.

evidence.description: Uploaded document evidence with normalized evidence types. An uploaded document is required for `counterfeit_merchandise`, `incorrect_amount` and `credit_not_processed` disputes, and for `duplicate_processing` and `paid_by_other_means` disputes whose payment proof is a document. A `cardholder_letter` document is required once the card already has two submitted disputes of the same reason against the same merchant within 30 days, for `merchandise_services_not_received` and `non_receipt_cash_at_atm`.

evidence_document_ids.description: Legacy document IDs to use as evidence, uploaded via `POST /issuing/card-disputes/documents`. Documents uploaded via `POST /documents` are rejected.

reason_details.description: Normalized reason-specific details for the dispute.

reason_for_partial_dispute.description: Reason the cardholder is disputing less than the full transaction amount. amount.description: The requested dispute amount in smallest currency unit.

card_transaction_id.description: The ID of the card transaction checked.

eligible.description: Whether the transaction is eligible for dispute creation.

existing_card_dispute_id.description: Existing active card dispute ID for this transaction, if present.

max_amount.description: The maximum currently disputable amount in smallest currency unit.

reasons.description: Reasons the transaction is not eligible.

cardholder_name_and_address_mismatch.description: The certification recorded with a response to a compelling-evidence pre-arbitration: whether the cardholder name and address the acquirer presented do not match your records.

compelling_evidence_reviewed_with_cardho.description: The certification recorded with a response to a compelling-evidence pre-arbitration: whether you contacted the cardholder, reviewed the acquirer's compelling evidence with them, and the cardholder continues to dispute the transaction.

created_at.description: When the event was created

id.description: The ID of the dispute event

response_action.description: The response intent recorded when this event was created. Includes recall, which is an internal close action and never accepted on POST /respond.

response_amount.description: Accepted-liability amount recorded for an accept_partial response, in smallest currency unit of the parent dispute's currency.

CardDisputeEventResponseAction.description: The response intent recorded on a dispute event. Superset of the actions POST /respond accepts: recall is the internal intent recorded when a submitted dispute is queued for network withdrawal and is never a valid /respond input.

card_dispute_event_id.description: The dispute event that submitted this evidence, linking it to the response that carried it.

created_at.description: When the evidence was created.

direction.description: Whether this evidence was supplied by the cardholder/platform or received from the network.

id.description: The ID of the dispute evidence.

narrative.example: The cardholder did not authorize this transaction and still has the card.

submitted_at.description: When this evidence was delivered to the network. Null while the evidence has never been sent; a dispute submission does not imply every later attachment was sent.

card_mailed_date.description: The date the card was mailed to the cardholder. Required when `fraud_type` is `card_not_received_as_issued`.

card_mailed_postal_code.description: The postal code the card was mailed to, at most 9 characters (for example `94107`, or `941071234` for a ZIP+4 code). Required when `fraud_type` is `card_not_received_as_issued`.

fraud_type.description: The cardholder-reported fraud subtype. Required. `acquirer_reported`, `merchant_misrepresentation` and `manipulation_of_account_holder` are retired: they can appear on disputes created before they were retired, but are rejected when creating a dispute, checking eligibility, or adding reason details. Visa reserves `acquirer_reported` for acquirers, and a fraud dispute certifies that the cardholder denies authorizing or participating in the transaction, so file a scam the cardholder took part in under a consumer dispute reason instead.

pin_preferring_card.description: Whether the card is a PIN-preferring chip card. Only used when `fraud_type` is `lost`, `stolen` or `card_not_received_as_issued`, and treated as `false` for a card without a chip. When omitted, Visa assumes `false`.

receipt_account_number_matches.description: Does the account number on the cardholder's receipt match the cardholder's account number or token? Required for incorrect-account-number disputes.

CardDisputeIncorrectAmountReasonDetails.description: Details for an incorrect-amount dispute. An uploaded document (the cardholder's receipt) is required before submission. The dispute amount must be less than the transaction amount, and no more than the transaction amount less `cardholder_receipt_amount`.

cardholder_receipt_amount.description:
The amount shown on the cardholder's receipt, in the smallest unit of the dispute currency.
This is the correct amount, as opposed to the amount actually charged. Required, and must leave the
dispute amount no more than the transaction amount less this amount.

quoted_price_difference.description: Is the dispute due to the difference between the price the merchant quoted and what it actually charged? Required when the transaction is with a travel and entertainment merchant (airline, car rental, lodging or passenger railway) and `cardholder_receipt_amount` differs from the transaction amount; otherwise stored but not sent to the network.

cardholder_did_not_agree_to_dcc.description: Does the issuer certify that the cardholder did not agree to dynamic currency conversion and did not make an active choice? Required when `currency_error` is `dynamic_currency_conversion`. Must be true: `false` would certify the cardholder agreed to the conversion the dispute claims they did not.

correct_currency.description: What currency should the transaction have been processed in? Required when `currency_error` is `currency_difference`. Must differ from the currency the merchant processed the transaction in.

currency_error.description: What was wrong with the transaction currency? Required.

CardDisputeIncorrectTransactionCodeReaso.description: Details for an incorrect-transaction-code dispute. The dispute amount must be less than the transaction amount.

transaction_code_error.description: How was the transaction code incorrect? Required.

resolution_prohibited_by_local_law.description: Is an attempt to resolve the dispute with the merchant prohibited by local law or regulations? CardDisputeReason.description: The reason for a card dispute, which selects the Visa dispute condition Column files: `fraud` (10), `no_authorization` (11), `incorrect_transaction_code` (12.2), `incorrect_currency` (12.3), `incorrect_account_number` (12.4), `incorrect_amount` (12.5), `duplicate_processing` (12.6.1), `paid_by_other_means` (12.6.2), `invalid_data` (12.7), `merchandise_services_not_received` (13.1), `canceled_recurring_transaction` (13.2), `not_as_described` (13.3), `damaged_or_defective_merchandise` (13.3), `quality_of_merchandise_or_services` (13.3), `terms_of_contract` (13.3, Visa Commercial Card Virtual Account transactions), `counterfeit_merchandise` (13.4), `misrepresentation` (13.5), `credit_not_processed` (13.6), `canceled_merchandise_or_services` (13.7), `original_credit_not_accepted` (13.8) and `non_receipt_cash_at_atm` (13.9). `other` has no Visa dispute condition and is not filed with the network.

CardDisputeReservationCertification.description: What the cardholder certifies about a canceled guaranteed reservation: `properly_canceled` (the cardholder properly canceled the guaranteed reservation), `attempted_cancellation_within_24_hours` (the cardholder attempted to cancel within 24 hours of delivery of the reservation confirmation) or `no_show_billed_for_more_than_one_day` (the merchant billed a no-show transaction for more than one day's accommodation or rental).

CardDisputeReturnMethod.description: How the cardholder returned merchandise to the merchant.

CardDisputeServiceType.description: The type of service a canceled-merchandise-or-services dispute concerns.

received_date.description: When did the cardholder receive the services? Required when the transaction was processed more than 113 days before submission.

terms_not_honored_details.description: How were the terms of the contract not honored by the merchant, or not as described? Required. Terms-of-contract disputes apply to Visa Commercial Card Virtual Account transactions.
terms_not_honored_details.example: The merchant did not deliver the services within the timeframe in the contract.

CardDisputeTransactionCodeError.description: How the transaction code was incorrect. idempotency_key.description: The idempotency key specified in the check transfer
